process: Goal 3 (physics) gets almost all the time. The physics is real (glass sag, glaze flow, plastic wire, tops, floating hulls), but each comes out as a tiny abstract demo on a slab, filmed with primitives, and rarely reaches a player in a form they can see and use. The wire bench is hidden behind an easel. Goal 1 (interactions people show friends) is barely moved: no creature took part in any of this session's films. Goal 2 (a proud traced release) has had no release since 2026-11-24, and #654 sits open. Goal 4/7 (rendering, materials): copper and glass are declared but don't read in the films, and the traced night has disc lamps and black clouds. Goal 5 (Lumi): Lumi's body at night is unreadable and the chick double persists, while mood.json says bored 1.0, lonely 1.0, annoyed 0.96, and the session's worth fell to 1.5 points. Goal 6 (motion): the measures are clean now, so close those todos. Goal 8: the posts have become one recipe (a material sim plus a close-up). The next session should take one of these sims into a scene with the creatures and a camera that can see it, rather than start a sixth bench.

animation.why: live_motion reports 10 of 10 creatures moving well. The films' motion is smooth (copper-wire-hook typical change 0.0001). But the lever in the wire film moves like a rigid box with no hand on it, and in the live strip Lumi barely moves over 2.4 s. No pose work was visible this session.

camera.why: Worse than at s142. In Jump in at the new wire bench the follow camera shows a wooden easel post filling half the frame, with Lumi and the bench behind it. Follow mode outside games frames a sleeping pig's back or a tree crown that fills half the view (#615). The dashboard progress shot this session is a featureless dark slab with a stick on it. Half the creature close-ups from live_motion show only a pig's back.

creatures.why: The crab, sheep and pigs read well up close, with hats. Lumi at night is a dark yellow spiky smudge among the easels with its pale chick double right beside it (#614), and from across the island you cannot pick out the main character.

fun.why: The wire bench works: holding 2 bent five joints to 1.25 rad each. But the player cannot see it: the follow camera stands behind an easel post (wire-1.png, wire-2.png). Jump in's key card lists 20 letter keys and none of 1-4 for the tops and the wire, so the only hint is a sentence in 'Things to try'. Firefly catch, Hide and seek and Berry race have not changed in many sessions.

lighting.why: In the raster view the night reads well: moon, stars, fireflies and the cottage's warm lamp pool. But the moon halo is a set of concentric bands, the clap shows as yellow paint splats on the ground, and in the path traced view every lamp is a flat opaque cream disc bigger than the cottage door, the clouds are pitch-black blobs and the image is heavy with grain. The noon sun-ball problem (#659) is still open and could not be checked at 05:00.

materials.why: The copper wire is declared Hikari.Copper, but in its film it is a flat red-orange tube with no highlight, on a plain grey slab next to an untextured orange box and a grey cylinder. The blown glass (first-glass-bubble.mp4, glass-glows-by-heat.mp4) is an opaque emissive yellow or red blob in full daylight, with no transmission and no glow on the sand. The tops are matte red and white. Nothing new shows what a path tracer can do.

performance.why: Frame median 3.7 ms, p95 7.8 ms at 30 fps; the wire bench costs 0.4 ms.

props.why: The generated assets (houses, mushrooms, trees, easels, TV) still carry the island, but every new prop this session is a primitive: Rect3f board, Cylinder pin, box lever.

style.why: The soft, clay-like island style holds, but every new film puts flat primitives (a grey slab on lime grass, a box lever) next to it, so the posts look like two different games.

ui.why: The panel is readable. But 'Feels annoyed. It still doesn't look right, and it bugs me.' sits in salmon red at the top for every visitor. The Jump in key card covers the lower middle of the view and is missing the keys this session added. 'Things to try' is a wall of text.

world.why: Same island, same layout. The new benches (tops, wire) are bare boards on bare ground between easels, with nothing around them that makes a place: no workshop corner, no tools, no story.

wow.why: The last ten posts: tops on a board, a wire on a board, hot glass on a pipe, a glazed jar, three logs on water, and five 'take that misses'. The host's judge scored the wire and tops as repeats (worth x0.22). None has a creature in it, a joke, or anything a stranger would forward. Lumi's own mood is bored 1.0 and lonely 1.0.

summary: At night the island is at its most charming in the raster view: a moon, fireflies everywhere, warm pools of lamplight by the cottage. This session's new toys are a turned top and a copper wire you bend with keys 2 and 3. Both run on real physics, and a player never gets to see them: in Jump in an easel post covers Lumi and the bench, and the films look like physics debug views (grey slab, orange box, red tube). The new work keeps being small simulations on a board. Each one is clever, none is a spectacle, and the host's judge already scores two of them as repeats.
